The connection to PostgreSQL: a pgx pool opened with the service, from DATABASE_URL, and where each module's tables live. With compose, a Postgres for development in compose.yaml, which the default DATABASE_URL points at. The annotations describe the tables to the blueprints that write their SQL (migrations, store).

```esquadro
blueprint postgres
```

## Works with

- **Requires** [app](../app/): the app must use them too.
- **Works with** [compose](../compose/) when the app uses them.

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pool_max` | int | `10` | Maximum number of connections in the pool; &lt;APP>_POOL_MAX overrides it. |
| `schemas` | list | `[]` | Modules whose tables live in a Postgres schema of their own, named after the module; the others use public. |

```esquadro
blueprint postgres {
  pool_max 10
}
```

## Annotations

| Where | Key | Type | |
|---|---|---|---|
| entity | `table` | name | Table name, when it should differ from the plural snake case name. |
| entity | `index` | fields | Columns of an index, e.g. index [name, status]. |
| entity | `unique_index` | fields | Columns of a unique index. |
| field | `column` | name | Column name, when it should differ from the snake case name. |

An annotation is written `@postgres(key value)` on the element.

## Go modules

- `github.com/jackc/pgx/v5` v5.7.1
